title: Job 40: Humble Thyself Before the Most High
body:
Read the chapter → [Job 40](/bible/job/40)

**[Job 40:1-5](/bible/job/40#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/job/40#v1)</sup> Moreover the Lord answered Job, and said,
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/job/40#v2)</sup> Shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct him? he that reproveth God, let him answer it.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/job/40#v3)</sup> Then Job answered the Lord, and said,
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/job/40#v4)</sup> Behold, I am vile; what shall I answer thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/job/40#v5)</sup> Once have I spoken; but I will not answer: yea, twice; but I will proceed no further.

- Moreover the Lord answered Job and said, shall he that contendeth with the Almighty instruct Him? He that reproveth God, let him answer it.
- Then Job answered the Lord and said, behold, I am vile; what shall I answer Thee? I will lay mine hand upon my mouth. Once have I spoken, but I will not answer; yea, twice, but I will proceed no further. Job humbles himself and puts his hand over his mouth.

**[Job 40:6-14](/bible/job/40#v6)**
> <sup>[6](/bible/job/40#v6)</sup> Then answered the Lord unto Job out of the whirlwind, and said,
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/job/40#v7)</sup> Gird up thy loins now like a man: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/job/40#v8)</sup> Wilt thou also disannul my judgment? wilt thou condemn me, that thou mayest be righteous?
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/job/40#v9)</sup> Hast thou an arm like God? or canst thou thunder with a voice like him?
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/job/40#v10)</sup> Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency; and array thyself with glory and beauty.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/job/40#v11)</sup> Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath: and behold every one that is proud, and abase him.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/job/40#v12)</sup> Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low; and tread down the wicked in their place.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/job/40#v13)</sup> Hide them in the dust together; and bind their faces in secret.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/job/40#v14)</sup> Then will I also confess unto thee that thine own right hand can save thee.

- Then the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind and said, gird up thy loins now like a man; I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto Me. Wilt thou also disannul My judgment? Wilt thou condemn Me, that thou mayest be righteous?
- Hast thou an arm like God? Or canst thou thunder with a voice like Him? Deck thyself now with majesty and excellency, and array thyself with glory and beauty. Cast abroad the rage of thy wrath, and behold every one that is proud, and abase him. Look on every one that is proud, and bring him low, and tread down the wicked in their place.
- The Most High is saying, if you can do these things, then can you disannul My judgment? Can you condemn the Most High, that you may be righteous? Can you bring down proud people? Can you get rid of the wicked?
- The thing is we get so high-minded sometimes, because of the little bit of knowledge that we have out of this Bible, and the wicked still rule over us. You better humble yourself. That is the whole purpose of the book of Job: learning how to humble yourself.

**[Job 40:15-24](/bible/job/40#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/job/40#v15)</sup> Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/job/40#v16)</sup> Lo now, his strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/job/40#v17)</sup> He moveth his tail like a cedar: the sinews of his stones are wrapped together.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/job/40#v18)</sup> His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/job/40#v19)</sup> He is the chief of the ways of God: he that made him can make his sword to approach unto him.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/job/40#v20)</sup> Surely the mountains bring him forth food, where all the beasts of the field play.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/job/40#v21)</sup> He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed, and fens.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/job/40#v22)</sup> The shady trees cover him with their shadow; the willows of the brook compass him about.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/job/40#v23)</sup> Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not: he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/job/40#v24)</sup> He taketh it with his eyes: his nose pierceth through snares.

- Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox. His strength is in his loins, and his force is in the navel of his belly. He moveth his tail like a cedar; the sinews of his stones are wrapped together. His bones are as strong pieces of brass; his bones are like bars of iron.
- He is the chief of the ways of God. He lieth under the shady trees, in the covert of the reed and fens. The willows of the brook compass him about. Behold, he drinketh up a river, and hasteth not; he trusteth that he can draw up Jordan into his mouth.
- That is actually talking about dinosaurs. Bishop did a class a while ago called The Beginning, Ending, and Midst of Times where he breaks down this portion in Job.
- He says his tail was like a cedar; a cedar is a very tall tree. There are not that many animals that have a tail the size of a cedar tree. A lot of people ask, where are the dinosaurs? Watch the video, The Beginning, Ending, and Midst of Times.
